task.question: Who was dismissed as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine on 21 July 2026?
task.evidence: 21 July – President Zelenskyy dismisses Oleksandr Syrskyi as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, replacing him with Mykhailo Drapatyi amidst protests demanding Syrskyi’s removal.

answer: FINAL: Oleksandr Syrskyi was dismissed as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine on 21 July 2026.

Oleksandr Stanislavovych Syrskyi [ a ] ( Ukrainian : Олександр Станіславович Сирський ; born 26 July 1965) is a Ukrainian military officer holding the rank of four-star general [ 9 ] who served as the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine from 2024 to 2026. In July 2026, Syrskyi reported that defense operations reduced Russia's territorial gains by more than half, and that 32,000 Russian soldiers had been killed or wounded in June 2026. [ 43 ] That month, Syrskyi's rivalry with the defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov came to a head. As a result, Fedorov was dismissed . [ 44 ] Fedorov's removal prompted protests across Ukraine calling for his reinstatement and for Syrskyi's removal . One protest leader accused the general of causing demoralization, sabotaging reforms, rewarding loyalty to himself and repressing soldiers; defenders of Syrskyi argued that hardships of the war were being unfairly taken out on the general and that Fedorov's plans for robotic warfare were unrealistic. [ 45 ] Ukrainian military members interviewed by the BBC lauded Syrski's great experience and key victories against Russia, but noted his outdated Soviet doctrine. [ 46 ] Syrskyi was replaced by Mykhailo Drapatyi on 21 July 2026. [ 14 ]
